## From lab to market

::: {.cards .roomy}
::: {.card}
[Spinout → acquisition]{.name}

**Adaptive3D** (Voit): tough 3D-printable rubbers for footwear to aerospace. Launched with UT Dallas's Venture Development Center; [acquired by Desktop Metal in 2021](https://news.utdallas.edu/faculty-staff/adaptive3d-sale-2021/).
:::

::: {.card}
[Faculty-founded company]{.name}

[**EnLiSense**](https://www.enlisense.com/) (Prasad, co-founder): non-invasive sweat-biomarker wearables; its CORTI platform was validated in her UT Dallas lab.
:::

::: {.card}
[Founder-scientist]{.name}

**Walker** brings several neurotechnology startups; his sleep-stimulation headband is already in professional sport.
:::

::: {.card}
[Students as innovators]{.name}

[**UTDesign**](https://utdesign.utdallas.edu/) capstones are proposed and mentored by companies. Example: a student team's athlete hydration wearable (2016).
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
~1 min. This is the slide for an innovation & entrepreneurship audience: four distinct pathways from research to product.
:::
